text:
anya: FYI the onboarding bulk-embeds sample is triggering 429 waves on first-run when users set batch=64 and concurrency=10. Repro with latest node SDK.

ravi: thanks. Is this token quota or concurrent request caps?

anya: looks like concurrent bursts + synced retries. We send 10 parallel POSTs, edge replies with Retry-After ~2s, and then clients retry almost in lockstep causing a second wave.

jo: quick peek: node SDK honours Retry-After for chat but not for bulkCreate. Also bulk backoff uses tiny jitter.

infra-bot: created ticket DX-1433 "onboard: bulk retry storms and SDK parity" assigned to @ravi

ravi: plan: SDK changes — (1) honour Retry-After header (seconds and HTTP-date) for embeds/bulk endpoints, (2) switch bulk endpoints to full jittered exponential backoff, (3) when acquiring concurrency slots, decrement by estimateTokens(batch) so big batches consume more slots.

paul: sample-app changes: default to batch=24 and concurrency=3 for first-run; add RW_ONBOARD_FAST=true opt-in for power users. Also add --warmup-mode flag in CLI.

anya: can we add an X-RW-CLIENT-SLOTS debug header so infra can correlate client-side bursts with edge limits without exposing keys?

ravi: yes, add X-RW-CLIENT-SLOTS in debug builds only. Also add e2e harness that runs a fake rate-limit server returning varied Retry-After to assert retries spread.

jo: parity note: ensure iOS/Android/Go implement same semantics (honour Retry-After + full jitter + token-estimate semaphore). I'll add checklist to DX-1433.

anya: after reducing defaults and enabling jitter locally, I reran and the second-wave 429 disappeared. If folks hit this, run with DEBUG=sdk:throttle and paste logs here. :thumbsup:
